key_insight: Fast AI models for vehicle aerodynamics need to transfer across vehicle classes, not just perform well on familiar designs. This paper targets adaptation using only a few new CFD simulations while preserving accuracy on the original vehicle class; the truncated abstract does not provide specific methods or results.
problem_solved: Neural aerodynamic surrogates struggle with zero-shot generalization to new vehicle classes, forcing costly, design-specific training campaigns.
method: Study transfer of pretrained aerodynamic surrogates across vehicle classes.
Target adaptation to a new class using a small number of CFD simulations.
Aim to preserve performance on the pretraining domain; implementation details are unavailable in the supplied excerpt.
impact: Better transfer could reduce the simulation data and retraining needed to deploy aerodynamic surrogates on new vehicle classes. Retaining original-domain accuracy would make pretrained models more reusable.
visual_elements: Transfer diagram: pretrained surrogate → few new CFD simulations → adapted surrogate.
Vehicle-class silhouettes illustrating the shift between training and target domains.
Conceptual chart of target-domain accuracy versus adaptation simulations, with no invented results.
Two evaluation gauges: new-class accuracy and original-class accuracy.
paper_title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics
paper_authors: Favour Nerrise, Julian Busch, Gurpreet Singh Hora, Martin Sipka, Danielle C. Maddix
